name: What is the difference between an in-law suite, ADU, and JADU in Southern California?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between an in-law suite, ADU, and JADU in Southern California?
mainEntity.text: What is the difference between an in-law suite, ADU, and JADU in Southern California?

acceptedAnswer.text: In Southern California, “in-law suite” is a general term, but ADU and JADU are the terms that matter for permitting and design. An ADU is a separate accessory dwelling unit with its own living functions, usually created as an attached addition, detached structure, or conversion. A JADU is smaller and typically carved out of existing living space inside the main house. The distinction affects size limits, privacy, kitchen requirements, and whether you need new utility systems. Homeowners often use the words interchangeably, but cities do not. Before starting a project, it is worth confirming whether the idea fits as a conversion, ADU, or JADU, because that choice affects budget, layout, and approval speed.
